summary: Fire Command: Zero-G is an AI-powered mission-control dashboard that turns NASA's microgravity combustion experiments into clear fire-safety insights for crewed spacecraft and future Moon and Mars habitats. It summarizes and ranks 12 NASA PSI combustion investigations (BASS, Saffire, SAME, FLEX, ACME and more) by relevance to a chosen habitat's oxygen, pressure, airflow and gravity, tagging each as prevention, detection or suppression. A machine-learning model trained on 190 real NASA runs (FLEX and Saffire-II) predicts how fast a fire grows and whether it goes out, explains the drivers in plain language, cites the exact NASA runs, and shows how confident it is. An AI assistant answers questions grounded in those runs, and a 3D fire drill lets anyone feel why acting in the first seconds matters. This matters because Moon bases will run at higher oxygen, where materials burn more easily — and the research to plan for that is scattered across decades of experiments.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Fire Command: Zero-G is a web dashboard that turns NASA's microgravity combustion experiments into fire-safety insights for crewed spacecraft and future Moon and Mars habitats.

- Which NASA research matters for your habitat? Pick the ISS, Artemis Gateway, a Lunar Habitat (34% O2, 56.5 kPa), a Mars transit ship or custom conditions. Twelve NASA PSI investigations (BASS, Saffire, SAME, DAFT, FLEX, FLEX-2, CFI, ACME's BRE / CFI-G / E-FIELD, SPICE, SLICE) re-rank for that habitat with a stated reason. Each is tagged prevention, detection or suppression, with what it studied, its hardware, what safety equipment it informs, a link to its NASA PSI record, and why it is or isn't in our model. Compare any two side by side, or ask the AI assistant to summarize one.

- Predict a fire. For any cabin condition, a model trained on 190 real NASA runs predicts the burning/spread rate with a likely range, the chance the flame keeps burning, and a risk index. A danger map shows where oxygen and airflow turn a fire dangerous and suggests a safer option.

- How sure are we? A confidence meter combines how many real NASA runs are near the chosen conditions, how wide the likely range is, and the model's tested accuracy, with a one-click jump to the closest real experiment.

- Interpret. Model explanations (SHAP) become plain sentences such as "oxygen pushes risk up noticeably". Every AI answer cites real NASA run IDs.

- Extract data. CSV download of every run behind the model, and a printable fire-safety report.

- Command Mode. A real-time, first-person fire emergency in a 3D station module: grab the extinguisher and aim; hesitate and the fire spreads to the equipment racks. Flame growth comes from the model; spreading and scoring are labelled game rules.

- Earth benefits. NASA spin-offs such as fine-water-mist extinguishers, smoke detection and firefighter gear.

HOW IT WORKS

NASA PSI experiment tables (FLEX, PSI-69: 274 rows read, 182 used; Saffire-II, PSI-99: 9 read, 8 used) are validated and mapped. Rows outside the app's ranges are rejected, never adjusted. Two facts the tables don't state were verified in NASA papers (FLEX burning rate is in mm²/s; Saffire-II's cabin was 22.1% O2 at 100.6 kPa). Gradient-boosting models, with quantile models for the likely range, are trained at startup, and SHAP explains each prediction. For each question, the 5 most similar real runs are retrieved and an LLM answers from them with validated citations; without a key or internet the app falls back to templates, so it never breaks.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

One place for students, researchers and engineers to find, compare and interpret NASA fire-safety research for a specific habitat, test a model built on real data, and download that data. Moon bases are expected to run at 30% oxygen or more, where materials burn much more easily, so planning fire safety for them starts with the research NASA has already done.

HOW IT IS CREATIVE

Instead of a static table of experiments, the dashboard ranks research for the place people will actually live, explains every number in plain language, admits when it is guessing, and lets anyone feel the physics: a flame that turns from a teardrop into a blue sphere as gravity drops, and a 3D fire drill where waiting even 20 seconds can cost the module.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

- Honesty: every number traces to a real NASA run; mock or simulated values are labelled; confidence is shown.

- Partial gravity: PSI has no partial-gravity combustion data, so Moon and Mars values are interpolated, flagged and given wider ranges.

- Accuracy: tested accuracy is modest (rate R² ≈ 0.22, extinction AUC ≈ 0.61), and the app shows this instead of hiding it.

- Accessibility: plain language for non-experts, depth for researchers, works on phones, works offline except for the optional AI.

- Scope: research and education tool, not operational fire-safety guidance.

TOOLS

TypeScript, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, three.js / react-three-fiber, Zustand; Python, FastAPI, scikit-learn, SHAP, pandas; Google Gemini (LLM and text-to-speech); hosted on Render.
